statuses.complete: Written, every code block executed against MuJoCo 3.14.0, labs tested in a browser.
statuses.draft: Written and executable, still being reviewed for depth and exercises.
statuses.planned: Syllabus only: objectives and scope are fixed, the lesson text is not written yet.

tiers.established: Established MuJoCo behavior, checked against the 3.14.0 documentation or source.
tiers.derivation: Mathematical derivation: follows from the stated assumptions.
tiers.implementation: Implementation detail: how MuJoCo (or this course's code) does it; may change between versions.
tiers.recommendation: Engineering recommendation: a judgement call, with its trade-off.
tiers.research: Research-level interpretation: an argument, not a measurement.
tiers.unverified: UNVERIFIED: could not be checked against a primary source; treat as a hypothesis.

levels.title: What is simulation?
levels.summary: What a physics simulator actually computes, how this course runs MuJoCo in two places, and what MuJoCo does not model.

lessons.title: What a physics simulator computes
objectives: Define state, dynamics, integration and timestep without jargon
Predict how a falling body's position depends on time, mass and gravity, then check it in MuJoCo
Explain why a simulator's output is an approximation even for a falling ball

lessons.title: Installation, versions and the two runtimes
objectives: Install MuJoCo 3.14.0 for Python and verify it

Set up headless rendering (EGL or OSMesa) on a server

lessons.title: What MuJoCo models, approximates and ignores
objectives: List the physical phenomena MuJoCo models natively and the ones it approximates
Recognise when a research question needs a different simulator or a real robot
Compare MuJoCo with other simulators by modelling assumptions, not by ranking

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint 0: predict, then simulate
checkpoint.task: Without running anything, write down how long the balls in ball_drop.xml (centre released at 1.0 m, radius 0.05 m) take to touch the floor and their speed at that moment. Then measure both in MuJoCo and explain the discrepancy in terms of the timestep and the contact model.
accept: Analytic answers within 1% (0.440 s and 4.32 m/s for a 0.95 m fall at g = 9.81 m/s^2)
Measured values with the measurement method stated
A one-paragraph explanation that names the timestep and contact softness

accept: Every array entry named with its unit
